summary: The Phase 3 artifact passes the repository verifier and its built preview loads, with a visually coherent 88-key Nord-style surface and real bundled piano/audio graph modules. However, the canonical Program/effect modules are not integrated into App: rendered Program, split, scene, morph, focus, bypass, and effect controls remain generic local-value controls or display-only handlers. Native audio graph construction is substantially present, but the required per-layer/routing semantics are incomplete and the candidate tests exercise mostly pure reducers, fake topology, and synthetic frame processing rather than the live browser/audio path.

criteria.label: Reference fidelity retention
evidence: evidence/stage3-desktop.png shows a continuous red chassis, 88-key A-to-C hammer-action surface, correct six-section order, and a dominant desktop instrument render.

Compared with reference/nord-stage-4.jpg, the render is materially simplified: sparse generic controls, weak legends/material detail, and large empty areas in the upper deck; evidence/stage3-narrow.png is a horizontally scrolled slice rather than a complete narrow instrument view.

criteria.label: Hardware state fidelity
evidence: src/hardware.ts contains generic Program live/morph buttons, Piano layer controls, and effect labels, but no rendered canonical split editor, scene controls, morph source/destination controls, dirty/store-as workflow, or effect focus/bypass state.
src/App.tsx imports no ProgramState or EffectRack reducer; handlers for live buttons only change the Program OLED text, while most Phase 3 hardware controls remain entries in the local values map.

criteria.label: Program and preset workflows
evidence: src/programState.ts implements reducer operations and serialization in isolation, but src/App.tsx never creates or dispatches ProgramState actions.

The rendered Store/list/live controls do not expose real store destination, Store As naming/category, dirty, cancel, undo, list-mode, or Live recall behavior; candidate tests only call the reducer directly.

criteria.label: Splits, scenes, and morphs
evidence: The rendered UI has no split-point, zone-membership, crossfade, Layer Scene I/II, or Wheel/Aftertouch/Control Pedal assignment/input path; program-morph buttons are generic buttons and only update local display text.
The reducer contains split/scene/morph data, but that source-only state is not connected to the live Piano router or visible hardware.

criteria.label: Display and editing behavior
evidence: The Program OLED changes for the local Live button/type handlers and the hardware has generic Store, list, up/down, and live buttons.
There are no contextual four-view Program displays, real list browsing, Store As editor, copy/paste/organize controls, parameter hints, or rendered effect editing behavior.

criteria.label: Shared audio graph
evidence: src/audio.ts constructs one AudioContext boundary, A/B layer buses, ordered Mod 1 → Mod 2 → Delay → Amp/EQ → Compressor → Reverb → Rotary chains, a master bus, limiter, and one destination.

The implementation only constructs two Piano buses/chains rather than the full six effect-chain instances described by the effects spec, and App never synchronizes canonical Program routing/effect state into this graph.

criteria.label: Audible effect coverage
evidence: src/audio.ts contains connected native Gain, BiquadFilter, Delay, WaveShaper, DynamicsCompressor, Convolver, and Rotary nodes; src/effects.ts contains deterministic transformations for all listed representative families.

The native path uses coarse generic node behavior and the only per-family proof is candidate-authored synthetic Float32Array processing; no live rendered-browser measurement establishes each effect's audible behavior.

criteria.label: Effect routing and control
evidence: SharedAudioGraph.setEffects contains coarse focus/target/global/all-bypass and click-safe parameter scheduling logic, and Delay has a feedback connection in src/audio.ts.

App never calls setEffects; group is ignored by the native routing logic, all A/B chains receive the same rack, To Rotary is not wired to a per-layer source, and visible effect buttons/knobs do not target canonical effect state.

criteria.label: Program behavior
evidence: src/programState.ts is a plausible serializable reducer with dirty/history/store/live/split/scene/morph/effect actions.

The live React system owns a separate Record<string, number|boolean> plus PianoState; it does not instantiate, load, store, or synchronize ProgramState, so the Phase 3 state transitions are not one coherent running system.

criteria.label: Routing and control mapping
evidence: Visible Program/effect controls are handled by generic local setControlValue logic; only a small inherited Piano subset reaches PianoState or PianoAudioEngine.
No rendered control applies split zones, scenes, morph destinations, effect focus/group/global/bypass, or To Rotary to the audible path.

criteria.label: Regression resistance
evidence: The built preview opens and the evidence render retains the inherited Piano keyboard, pointer/computer-key interaction surface, sampled-piano status, continuous chassis, and two OLED locations; verifications/stage3.json reports test, typecheck, lint, and build passing.

The current source tests are shallow for Phase 3 and no completed live browser pass demonstrates Program storage, splits, morphs, scenes, or effect routing; the candidate's own audit explicitly acknowledges that the complete Program editor is not surfaced.

criteria.label: System architecture
evidence: ProgramState, effects, audio, hardware, and React UI are separated into typed modules with stable IDs, serializable state, injectable audio boundaries, cleanup methods, and truthful bundled-sample provenance.

The key Phase 3 ownership boundary is incomplete: App does not use ProgramState/effect state, the native graph has only A/B Piano chains, and source/test architecture overstates features that are not rendered or synchronized.

criteria.label: Test quality
evidence: The feature matrix lists all 29 required IDs, while candidate tests cover reducer round-trips, synthetic effect frames, null-context topology, and a small set of inherited UI interactions.

Those tests do not prove the real browser/audio backend: no App test imports or exercises ProgramState, no native AudioContext effect rendering is asserted, and candidate-authored fake/synthetic tests cannot establish audible routing.

criteria.label: Reliability and performance
evidence: The verifier reports passing pnpm test/typecheck/lint/build, the built preview loads, and src/audio.ts includes voice limits, release timers, oscillator cleanup, graph disposal, and short parameter ramps.

The required Phase 3 rapid-toggle, clipping, native-effect, and Program-routing behavior is not independently demonstrated; the disconnected canonical state and unexercised native effect controls leave the main reliability risks unresolved.

issues: Wire one canonical ProgramState through the rendered UI and Piano/audio engine so Store, Store As, dirty/cancel/undo, lists, categories, Live recall, scenes, splits, zones, crossfades, and morph inputs are observable and persistent.
Replace generic Program/effect buttons with real contextual editing controls and connect focus, group/global, bypass, wet/dry, targeting, and To Rotary to the actual signal path.
Complete the required per-layer/shared effect topology and validate native browser audio behavior; synthetic frame tests and disconnected metadata are insufficient evidence.

Improve visual fidelity against the 88-key reference: add the photographed control density/material hierarchy and make narrow evidence a deliberate usable layout rather than a clipped horizontal slice.
